title: Ratify the HumbleStudio product charter and 12-month roadmap
summary: Convert the existing product, professionalization, and assurance work into one repository-owned charter for internal visual product, design, diagram, and proposal workspace.
acceptance_criteria: Ratify the repository purpose as: internal visual product, design, diagram, and proposal workspace.
Name the primary user, primary job, top three user outcomes, and intentionally unsupported use cases.

Adopt a 12-month product horizon grounded in the existing flagship scope: Deliver one polished standalone product milestone for internal visual product, design, diagram, and proposal workspace: open repository-backed product truth, edit a screen or diagram, review a proposal, hand it to Codex, and reconcile implementation. The slice must prove user value, UI/UX quality, performance, accessibility, recovery, and the declared monetization or non-monetization posture.
Define one north-star outcome, a small set of supporting signals, and guardrails that prevent metric gaming.
Separate user value, engineering maturity, operational readiness, and business value instead of using one percentage.
Record the monetization posture as `internal-now-optional-commercialization-later` and the evidence required before it can change.
Record the current fusion posture: Likely destination for selected Architect capabilities; Board and design editing remain its core.
Define product boundaries, owned data, external dependencies, and the responsibilities that must remain outside this repository.
Define lifecycle disposition, review cadence, and explicit criteria to invest, maintain, consolidate, freeze, or retire.
Map current Waves 1–9 tickets to product outcomes and identify duplicates, research-only work, and gaps.
Create a repository-owned 12-month roadmap with no more than three active product bets.
Define accessibility, localization, privacy, support, and recovery expectations at product level.
Define which user-facing claims can be public and which remain private or internal.
Identify assumptions that require user, device, hardware, business, or operational evidence.
Document the smallest valuable release and the smallest reversible experiment.
Define decision rights and the changes that always require Jan.
Publish human-readable and machine-readable charter artifacts.
Refresh repo-owned status to reference the charter without replacing current operational truth.
Validate the charter against the current repository revision and open work.
Complete warning-free repository validation.

blocked_by.reason: The capstone scope depends on reviewed earlier-wave foundations.

trigger.source_ref: Jan requested Wave 10 as the largest and most thorough final planning wave across the entire portfolio.

agent_notes: Portfolio Capstone and Operating System Wave 10.
Non-scope: do not release, deploy, merge products, mutate external data, delete, restore, or enable monetization from this planning ticket.
Alternative considered and rejected: adding more disconnected ambitious features without charter, capacity, assurance, and product evidence would make the portfolio less trustworthy.
Wave 10 is a realization and rationalization layer, not a reason to keep expanding the backlog indefinitely.
Fusion posture: Likely destination for selected Architect capabilities; Board and design editing remain its core..
Wave 11 execution reconciliation: `required-prerequisite`. Use the Wave 11 implementation program as the delivery entry point while preserving this ticket's evidence and intent.

Wave 12 deep reassessment: decision `retain-charter-input`, relevance `next`, current priority `medium`, execution gate `use as governing context, not another parallel backlog`. Portfolio and product charters remain decision inputs, while Wave 11 and Wave 12 own implementation and completion.
Wave 13 human-validation reassessment: `retain-product-charter-input` / `next` / priority `high`. Product role, lifecycle, and investment decisions frame the validation program.

Final Wave 14 validity review: `valid`; publication `publish-after-fresh-reconciliation`; implementation sequence `after-sudoku`. Product role, lifecycle, and investment decisions frame the validation program.
